name: Structured telemetry and metrics
description: FADE currently produces human-readable logs (progress/learned), but not machine-usable telemetry. Telemetry is required to (a) measure efficiency and reliability, (b) improve model selection/complexity estimation, (c) support dashboards and multi-repo operations, and (d) provide research-grade evidence of impact.

userStories.title: Emit structured events for key lifecycle actions
userStories.description: FADE writes append-only JSONL events for run lifecycle, PRD/story transitions, model selection, signals, and errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Each run writes `fade/runs/<run_id>/events.jsonl` as newline-delimited JSON objects.
Event schema includes: `ts`, `run_id`, `repo`, `event_type`, and a `data` object for details.
At minimum, emit events for: run_start, run_stop, prd_start, prd_end, story_start, story_end, model_selected, signal_received, blocked, regression_start, regression_end, error.
Events are appended in chronological order and never rewritten.
Events do not contain secrets (no API keys, tokens, or credential-like strings).

userStories.title: Provide operator metrics derived from telemetry
userStories.description: Operators can quickly understand throughput, failures, retries, and model usage.
acceptanceCriteria: Command `fade metrics` summarizes the last N runs across the current repo (and workspace later): total stories completed, failures, BLOCKED count, regressions run, average story duration, model usage breakdown.
Command `fade metrics --run <run_id>` prints per-run metrics including per-story durations and outcomes.
Metrics output is deterministic and readable (table-like).
